subject: Cardiology
content: Cardiology focuses on prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up of diseases affecting the heart and circulatory system.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: The cardiovascular system consists of the heart and blood vessels and circulates blood to deliver oxygen and nutrients and remove metabolic waste.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: The heart has four chambers: right and left atria and right and left ventricles. Their coordinated activity supports pulmonary and systemic circulation.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: The cardiac valves help maintain one-way blood flow through the heart. The major valves are tricuspid, pulmonary, mitral, and aortic valves.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: The coronary arteries supply blood to the heart muscle. Reduced coronary blood flow can cause myocardial ischemia.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: The cardiac conduction system coordinates electrical activation of the heart and supports organized atrial and ventricular contraction.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: The cardiac cycle consists of alternating phases of ventricular filling and contraction that generate forward blood flow.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: Cardiac output is the volume of blood pumped by the heart per unit time and is determined by heart rate and stroke volume.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: Blood pressure reflects the force exerted by circulating blood on arterial walls and is influenced by cardiac output and vascular resistance.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: Heart rate is the number of cardiac cycles per minute and is regulated by intrinsic conduction activity and autonomic influences.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: Hypertension is persistently elevated blood pressure and is an important risk factor for cardiovascular disease, stroke, kidney disease, and other complications.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: Risk factors for hypertension include unhealthy diet, high sodium intake, physical inactivity, excess body weight, tobacco exposure, alcohol use, age, and genetic factors.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: Uncontrolled hypertension can damage the heart, brain, kidneys, and blood vessels and increase the risk of cardiovascular events.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: Healthy diet, regular physical activity, maintaining a healthy body weight, avoiding tobacco, and reducing excess alcohol can help prevent or control hypertension.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: Coronary artery disease occurs when disease in the coronary arteries reduces blood supply to the heart muscle, commonly due to atherosclerotic plaque.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: Atherosclerosis involves accumulation of plaque within arterial walls and can narrow or obstruct arteries supplying the heart and other organs.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: Angina is chest discomfort caused by inadequate oxygen supply to the heart muscle relative to its demand, often related to coronary artery disease.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: Acute coronary syndrome describes a group of conditions caused by acute reduction of coronary blood flow and includes unstable angina and myocardial infarction.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: Myocardial infarction occurs when prolonged myocardial ischemia causes injury and death of heart muscle cells, usually because of acute coronary artery obstruction.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: Possible symptoms include chest discomfort, shortness of breath, sweating, nausea, and pain or discomfort that may spread to the arm, shoulder, jaw, or back.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: Heart failure is a clinical syndrome in which the heart cannot adequately meet the body's needs or can do so only with elevated filling pressures.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: Common manifestations of heart failure include breathlessness, fatigue, reduced exercise tolerance, and fluid retention such as peripheral edema.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: Coronary artery disease, hypertension, diabetes, and other cardiovascular conditions can contribute to the development of heart failure.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: Cardiac arrhythmias are abnormalities of heart rhythm that can result from disturbances in impulse formation or conduction.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: Atrial fibrillation is an irregular atrial rhythm that can reduce coordinated atrial contraction and increase the risk of thromboembolic stroke.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: Bradycardia refers to an abnormally slow heart rate and may be physiological or associated with conduction disease, medications, or other conditions.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: Tachycardia refers to an abnormally rapid heart rate and may arise from sinus mechanisms or abnormal cardiac rhythms.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: Valvular heart disease occurs when one or more heart valves become narrowed, fail to close properly, or otherwise interfere with normal blood flow.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: Aortic stenosis is narrowing of the aortic valve opening, which increases resistance to left ventricular outflow.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: Mitral regurgitation occurs when the mitral valve does not close effectively, allowing blood to flow backward from the left ventricle into the left atrium during systole.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: Cardiomyopathies are diseases of the heart muscle that can impair mechanical or electrical function and may lead to heart failure or arrhythmias.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: Dilated cardiomyopathy is characterized by ventricular dilation and impaired systolic function that cannot be explained by abnormal loading conditions alone.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy involves abnormal thickening of the heart muscle and can cause impaired filling, outflow obstruction, arrhythmias, or sudden cardiac death.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: Pericarditis is inflammation of the pericardium and may cause chest pain and other symptoms depending on the cause and severity.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: Pericardial effusion is accumulation of fluid in the pericardial space. Large or rapidly developing effusions can impair cardiac filling.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: Cardiac tamponade occurs when pericardial pressure compromises cardiac filling and can produce life-threatening circulatory impairment.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: Infective endocarditis is infection of the endocardial surface, commonly involving heart valves, and can cause systemic complications.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: Congenital heart disease refers to structural or functional abnormalities of the heart present from birth and includes many different conditions.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: Atrial and ventricular septal defects are congenital openings between heart chambers that can alter normal blood flow depending on their size and location.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: An electrocardiogram records the electrical activity of the heart and can help evaluate rhythm, conduction, ischemia, and other cardiac abnormalities.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: Echocardiography uses ultrasound to assess cardiac structures and function, including chambers, valves, ventricular function, and blood flow.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: Cardiac biomarkers can provide biochemical evidence of myocardial injury and are used with clinical assessment and other investigations.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: Stress testing evaluates cardiac response to increased physiological demand and can help assess suspected coronary disease in selected patients.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: Major cardiovascular risk factors include tobacco use, unhealthy diet, physical inactivity, hypertension, diabetes, abnormal blood lipids, and obesity.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: Regular physical activity, healthy diet, avoidance of tobacco, and management of blood pressure, blood glucose, and blood lipids reduce cardiovascular risk.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: Stroke occurs when blood flow to part of the brain is interrupted or when a blood vessel in the brain ruptures. Cardiovascular risk factors contribute substantially to stroke risk.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: Cardiac arrest is cessation of effective cardiac activity and requires immediate recognition, cardiopulmonary resuscitation, and appropriate emergency response.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: Shock is a state of inadequate tissue perfusion and may result from cardiac, hypovolemic, distributive, or obstructive causes.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: Percutaneous coronary intervention can restore coronary blood flow in selected patients with significant coronary obstruction, particularly in acute coronary syndromes.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: Cardiac rehabilitation combines exercise, education, risk-factor management, and psychosocial support to help people recover and reduce future cardiovascular risk.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: Cardiovascular diseases are a major global cause of death and include conditions affecting the heart and blood vessels.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.

subject: Cardiology
content: Cardiovascular care should consider the patient's symptoms, risks, preferences, functional goals, comorbidities, and access to appropriate preventive and therapeutic services.
license: Source-specific reuse terms apply; this record is an original paraphrase with attribution.
